definition: Imbalance between AI developers and affected populations in access to information, resources, and decision-making authority. Encompasses information asymmetry (developers know what systems do; users and communities do not) and power asymmetry (developers set terms; affected populations bear consequences).
rationale_for_coinage: Skeptics see power and information asymmetry as the core structural problem in AI governance. Accelerationists may use 'asymmetry' to mean competitive advantage. The bare term conceals whether the speaker sees asymmetry as a problem to fix or an advantage to exploit.

do_not_confuse_with.note: Capabilities scaling describes AI system growth; power asymmetry describes the distributional consequences of that growth on different populations.

contested_aspects: Whether information asymmetry can be resolved through transparency alone
Whether power asymmetry is inherent to technological development or specific to current institutional arrangements
